q: What made Freyssinet's Plougastel Bridge (1930) notable when it was completed?
o: The longest reinforced-concrete arch bridge, with three 187 m spans
The first suspension bridge built entirely of prestressed steel
The first bridge assembled from precast concrete box girders
The longest cable-stayed bridge in Europe of its time
n: At its completion, the Plougastel Bridge (1930) was the largest reinforced-concrete bridge, with three spans of 187 meters each.

q: Charles Rennie Mackintosh (1868–1928) was a leading figure in which movements?
o: Arts and Crafts and Art Nouveau
n: The Scottish architect and designer Mackintosh was a prominent figure in the Arts and Crafts movement and Art Nouveau style.

q: Which architect is known to have said: "Seek truth in beauty, and beauty in truth"?
n: This dictum, along with "Architecture must be rooted in place and culture," belongs to Moshe Safdie (b. 1938).

q: Inigo Jones (1573–1652) brought classical architecture to Britain under the influence of which Italian architect?
n: Jones, an English architect who introduced classical architecture to Britain, was influenced by the Italian Renaissance and the works of Palladio.

q: Which architect is associated with the words: "I don't divide architecture, landscape and gardening; to me they are one"?
n: This dictum, and "Any architectural work that does not express serenity is an error," belong to Louis Barragán (1902–1988).

q: Eero Saarinen (1910–1961) was the son of which architect?
n: Eero Saarinen was a Finnish American architect and son of Eliel Saarinen, known for innovative sculptural designs like the TWA Flight Center and the Gateway Arch.

q: In which country did Kenzo Tange (1913–2005) lead post-war reconstruction and urban planning?
n: Tange, a Japanese architect who fused traditional Japanese styles with modernism, played a pivotal role in post-war reconstruction and urban planning in Japan, reflecting the influence of Le Corbusier.

q: Which architect or designer is credited with the line: "The details are not the details. They make the design"?
n: "The details are not the details. They make the design" is a dictum of Charles Eames (1907–1978).

q: The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture is Juan Nakpil, Pablo Antonio and who else?
ref: Architectural Groups (Local), The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture
n: The Triumvirate of Modern Philippine Architecture consists of Juan Nakpil, Pablo Antonio, and Leandro Locsin.

q: Which Art Deco skyscraper in New York is William Van Alen (1883–1954) best known for?
n: Van Alen's work epitomizes the Art Deco style with its ornate detailing and spire, best known for designing the Chrysler Building in New York City.

q: Which architect is associated with the words: "not only the director, but... the composer"?
n: This dictum, along with "Architecture and sculpture are two rivers in which the same water flows," belongs to Santiago Calatrava (b. 1951).

q: Which architect said: "Buildings should be good neighbors"?
n: "Buildings should be good neighbors" is a dictum of Cesar Pelli (1926–2019).

q: Which architect is on record with the statement: "Form follows function"?
n: "Form follows function" is a famous dictum of Louis Sullivan (1856–1924).

q: Peter Behrens (1868–1940), a pioneer of industrial design, helped develop which business idea through his work for AEG?
n: The German architect and designer Behrens was a pioneer of modern industrial design and played a significant role in the development of corporate identity, as with the AEG Turbine Factory.

q: Which of these was NOT a director of the Bauhaus?
n: The Bauhaus's directors were Walter Gropius, Hannes Meyer, and Ludwig Mies van der Rohe. Marcel Breuer was a Master Teacher (Furniture), not a director.

q: At which university did James Stirling (1926–1992) design the Engineering Building?
n: Stirling's Engineering Building at the University of Leicester (1963) was recognized for its innovative use of space and materials, marking a departure from traditional academic architecture.

q: Juan F. Nakpil, the 'Dean of Filipino Architects', holds which distinction?
o: The designer of the Chrysler Building
The first National Artist for Architecture
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Juan F. Nakpil
n: Juan F. Nakpil was regarded as the 'Dean of Filipino Architects' and was the first National Artist for Architecture, championing a distinctly Filipino architecture.

q: Which architect said: "Architecture begins where engineering ends"?
n: "Architecture begins where engineering ends" and "Art and technology—a new unity" are dicta of Walter Gropius (1883–1969).

q: Daniel Burnham (1846–1912) was a leading figure in which urban planning movement?
n: Burnham was a leading figure in the City Beautiful movement, promoting beautification and monumental grandeur in urban planning, notably through the Plan of Chicago (1909).

q: Which architect is credited with the line: "Beauty is the harmony of purpose and form"?
n: "Beauty is the harmony of purpose and form" is a dictum of Alvar Aalto (1898–1976).

q: Which architect is known to have said: "There are 360 degrees. Why stick to one?"?
n: "There are 360 degrees. Why stick to one?" is a dictum of Zaha Hadid (1950–2016).

q: Alvar Aalto's humanistic modernism is known for integrating what?
n: The Finnish architect and designer Aalto is known for his humanistic approach to modernism, integrating natural materials and organic forms across architecture, furniture, and glassware design.

q: Francisco Mañosa spent his career adapting the Bahay Kubo and which other traditional Filipino house into modern buildings?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa
n: Mañosa spent his career refining the Bahay Kubo and Bahay na Bato into modern structures, championing indigenous materials like bamboo, rattan, coconut, and capiz shells.

q: Which architect said: "Architecture is a way of seeing, thinking, and questioning our world and our place in it"?
n: This dictum belongs to Thom Mayne (b. 1944).

q: Where was the 1988 'Deconstructivist Architecture' exhibition held?
n: The Deconstructivists were the only architects featured in the seminal 1988 MoMA exhibition 'Deconstructivist Architecture,' curated by Philip Johnson and Mark Wigley.

q: Which architect is credited with the line: "A house is like a flowerpot"?
n: "A house is like a flowerpot" and "A building can be designed only when the designer knows exactly how it will be used" are dicta of Richard Neutra (1892–1970).

q: Francisco 'Bobby' Mañosa (National Artist, 2018) was the most vocal advocate of which approach?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa
n: Mañosa was the most vocal advocate for Neo-vernacular architecture, famously stating 'I design Filipino, nothing else.'

q: Which of these is a project of Skidmore, Owings & Merrill (SOM)?
n: SOM's notable works include Willis Tower (formerly Sears Tower), Burj Khalifa (the tallest structure globally, with SOM as lead architect), and One World Trade Center.

q: Which major complex, a masterclass in Brutalist architecture, did Leandro Locsin design?
o: The National Library of the Philippines
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Leandro V. Locsin
n: Locsin designed the iconic Cultural Center of the Philippines (CCP) complex, which remains a masterclass in Brutalist architecture.

q: Joseph Paxton designed the Crystal Palace, a pioneering prefabricated iron-and-glass building, for which event?
n: Paxton, an English gardener, architect, and engineer, designed the Crystal Palace, a pioneering example of prefabricated iron and glass architecture, built for the Great Exhibition of 1851.

q: Which architect is on record with the statement: "The city is an addictive machine from which there is no escape"?
n: "The city is an addictive machine from which there is no escape" and "Form follows performance" are dicta of Rem Koolhaas (b. 1944).

q: Which architect mentored many of the Metabolists and used his prestige to give them a platform?
n: Kenzo Tange was the professor and mentor to many of the core Metabolist members, using his international prestige to give the younger Metabolists a platform at the World Stage 1960.

q: Which building was Antoni Gaudí's first major commission?
n: Gaudí designed his first major commission, Casa Vincens in Barcelona, using a Gothic Revival style that set a precedent for his future works.

q: Zaha Hadid's Guangzhou Opera House, the 'double pebble', was inspired by what?
o: Ocean waves breaking on a shore
Sand dunes shaped by the wind
n: The Guangzhou Opera House, known as the 'double pebble,' was inspired by river stones smoothed by erosion.

q: Which architect or planner is associated with the words: "Make no little plans; they have no magic to stir men's blood"?
n: "Make no little plans; they have no magic to stir men's blood" and "Make big plans; aim high in hope and work..." are dicta of Daniel Burnham (1846–1912).

q: Which architect said: "Architecture is the art of how to waste space"?
n: "Architecture is the art of how to waste space" and "All architects want to live beyond their deaths" are dicta of Philip Johnson (1906–2005).

q: Which of these did National Artist Francisco 'Bobby' Mañosa design?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Francisco "Bobby" Mañosa
n: Mañosa's notable works include The Coconut Palace ('Tahanang Pilipino'), Pasay City, showcasing the versatility of the coconut tree, as well as the EDSA Shrine and Amanpulo Resort.

q: Which pensionado, the youngest of the group, designed the Manila City Hall and the Agriculture and Finance Buildings?
n: Antonio Toledo, the youngest pensionado, designed the Manila City Hall and the Agriculture and Finance Building.

q: Robert Venturi (1925–2018) challenged modernist purity by arguing for what in architecture?
n: Venturi challenged modernist principles, advocating for 'complexity and contradiction' in architecture, as seen in the Vanna Venturi House.

q: Which architect made the remark: "Always design a thing by considering it in its next larger context—a chair in a room, a room in a house, a house in an environment"?
n: This dictum belongs to Eero Saarinen (1910–1961).

q: Which essay is Adolf Loos (1870–1933) best known for?
n: Loos's essay 'Ornament and Crime' argued that removing ornament was a sign of cultural evolution, and emphasized functionality and simplicity.

q: Which architect said: "Each new situation requires a new architecture"?
n: "Each new situation requires a new architecture" is a dictum of Jean Nouvel (b. 1945).

q: Jose Maria Zaragoza's Sto. Domingo Church fuses the Spanish Colonial 'Mission style' with which other style?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Jose Maria Zaragoza
n: Sto. Domingo Church, Quezon City—arguably Zaragoza's most famous work and a declared National Cultural Treasure—is a fusion of Spanish Colonial 'Mission style' and Modernism.

q: Which architect is credited with the line: "Form follows beauty"?
n: "Form follows beauty" and "Architecture is invention" are dicta of Oscar Niemeyer (1907–2012).

q: Which building shows Adolf Loos's minimalist, rationalist design?
n: The Steiner House in Vienna, Austria, exemplifies Loos's minimalist aesthetic and rationalist design principles.

q: Which of these is a notable work of Le Corbusier (1887–1965)?
n: Le Corbusier's notable works include Villa Savoye, France; Unité d'Habitation, Marseille; Notre-Dame du Haut, Ronchamp; and Chandigarh, India.

q: Geoffrey Bawa (1919–2003) is revered as the 'Father of' which movement?
n: Bawa is widely revered as the 'Father of Tropical Modernism,' proving that Modernist principles could be adapted to the tropical, humid, culturally rich context of South and Southeast Asia.

q: Who make up the Pioneer Triumvirate that laid the foundations of the architecture profession in the Philippines?
o: Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, and Juan Arellano
Juan Nakpil, Pablo Antonio, and Leandro Locsin
Carlos Barretto, Antonio Toledo, and Tomas Mapua
Jose Maria Zaragoza, Carlos Arguelles, and Edmundo Lucero
n: The Pioneer Triumvirate—Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, and Juan Arellano—are credited with establishing the foundations of the profession in the early 20th century.

q: In 2004, Zaha Hadid (1950–2016) made history by becoming what?
o: The first woman to lead the Bauhaus
The first woman inducted into the AIA
The first woman to design a skyscraper in New York
The first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize
n: In 2004, Zaha Hadid became the first woman to win the Pritzker Architecture Prize.

q: Which architect is credited with the line: "A house is a machine for living in"?
n: "A house is a machine for living in" is one of Le Corbusier's (1887–1965) famous dicta.

q: Which aerospace software did Frank Gehry use to realize his sculptural forms?
n: As a leader of Deconstructivism, Gehry revolutionized the field by using aerospace software (CATIA) to design buildings that look like they are in motion.

q: Which architect said, "Architecture is art, but it is art contaminated by many other things"?
n: Renzo Piano uses this line to say architecture must answer to use, cost, society and technique, not only to art.

q: Which campus, the largest collection of Art Deco buildings in Manila, did Pablo S. Antonio design?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Pablo S. Antonio
n: The Far Eastern University (FEU) Campus, Manila, designed by Pablo S. Antonio, is considered the largest collection of Art Deco structures in Manila, featuring Nicanor Reyes Hall, the Engineering building, and the Administration building.

q: Which architect said: "There is a powerful need for symbolism, and that means the architecture must have something that appeals to the human heart"?
n: This dictum, along with "The city must be subject to growth, decay and renewal," belongs to Kenzo Tange (1913–2005).

q: Which design approach did Zaha Hadid pioneer with her partner Patrik Schumacher?
n: Alongside her partner Patrik Schumacher, Hadid pioneered Parametricism, pushing the construction industry to develop new methods for curved concrete and non-linear geometries.

q: Which architect is credited with the line: "Architecture is always political"?
n: "Architecture is always political" and "Form follows profit is the aesthetic principle of our times" are dicta of Richard Rogers (1933–2021).

q: What idea does Aldo Rossi's book 'L'architettura della città' (1966) stress?
o: The elimination of all historical references
The importance of historical continuity in urban planning
The importance of ornament in design
n: Rossi's book emphasizes the importance of historical continuity in urban planning, tied to his concept of 'Collective Memory'—that urban form preserves the history and identity of its citizens.

q: Leandro Locsin's Church of the Holy Sacrifice at UP Diliman was the first Catholic church in the Philippines to have what?
o: A circular design and a thin-shell concrete dome
A bell tower in the Baroque style
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Leandro V. Locsin
n: The Church of the Holy Sacrifice, UP Diliman, is the first Catholic church in the country with a circular design and a thin-shell concrete dome.

q: Which architect or designer is associated with the words: "To create, one must first question everything"?
n: This dictum belongs to Eileen Gray (1878–1976).

q: Which structural device did Antoni Gaudí use to make self-supporting forms without flying buttresses?
n: Gaudí pioneered the use of the catenary arch—an upside-down hanging chain model—to create self-supporting structures without the need for traditional flying buttresses.

q: Which architect, answering Mies van der Rohe, said "Less is a bore"?
n: "Less is a bore" and "More is More" are famous dicta of Robert Venturi (1925–2018).

q: Which Deconstructivist architect designed the Parc de la Villette in Paris?
n: Bernard Tschumi is known for the Parc de la Villette project among the Deconstructivists.

q: Which architect is known to have said: "Architecture has its own realm. It has a special physical relationship with life"?
n: This dictum belongs to Peter Zumthor (b. 1943).

q: Which glass structure at a Paris museum is I.M. Pei (1917–2019) famous for?
n: I.M. Pei's Louvre Pyramid (1989) is a glass and metal pyramid serving as the main entrance to the Louvre Museum, blending contemporary design with its historic surroundings.

q: Michael Graves (1934–2015) designed over 2,000 household items. Which is the most famous?
o: The Alessi kettle with a bird whistle
n: Graves designed over 2,000 household items, including the iconic Alessi teakettle with a bird-shaped whistle, and integrated classical elements with modern design, whimsy, and color.

q: Which architect said: "Architecture is not based on concrete and steel, and the elements of the soil. It's based on wonder"?
n: This dictum belongs to Daniel Libeskind (b. 1946).

q: Pier Luigi Nervi (1891–1979) is known for joining engineering precision and elegance in which material?
n: Nervi was renowned for his innovative use of reinforced concrete, combining engineering precision with architectural elegance, and often featured thin-shell structures.

q: Which Filipino National Artist is credited with the line: "buildings should be planned with austerity in mind... simple in design but dignified, true to a purpose"?
n: This dictum belongs to Pablo Antonio (1901–1975).

q: Which architect is known to have said: "An architect does not need to spend his whole career making monuments for rich people"?
n: This dictum belongs to Shigeru Ban (b. 1957).

q: Which SOM architect's Lever House (1952) brought the firm new recognition?
n: In 1952, Gordon Bunshaft pushed SOM toward a new level of architectural recognition with his design for the Lever House, a curtain-walled office block in the international style.

q: Louis Kahn (1901–1974) is known for monumental designs built around what?
n: Kahn's work is characterized by its use of natural light and geometric forms, as seen in the Salk Institute for Biological Studies and the Kimbell Art Museum.

q: Jose Maria Zaragoza (National Artist, 2014) was the master of which architectural specialty?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Jose Maria Zaragoza
n: Zaragoza was the master of Ecclesiastical Architecture, defining the modern Catholic aesthetic in the Philippines during the mid-20th century.

q: Eugène Freyssinet (1879–1962) is celebrated as the father of which construction innovation?
n: The French structural engineer Freyssinet is celebrated as the father of prestressed concrete, revolutionizing the use of concrete for longer spans and more daring forms.

q: Which Victor Horta building is considered the first true Art Nouveau building?
n: Horta's Hôtel Tassel, Brussels, is considered the first true Art Nouveau building.

q: Which architect is known to have said: "A room is not a room without natural light"?
n: "A room is not a room without natural light" and "Even a brick wants to be something" are dicta of Louis Kahn (1901–1974).

q: Santiago Calatrava (b. 1951) draws his sculptural structures mainly from what?
n: Calatrava, trained as both architect and engineer, bases forms like the Turning Torso on the human spine and on skeletons, birds and plants.

q: Which architect is associated with the words: "Ornament is crime"?
n: "Ornament is crime" is the famous dictum of Adolf Loos (1870–1933).

q: Which Frank Lloyd Wright house was built over a waterfall in Pennsylvania in 1935?
n: Fallingwater (1935) is a house in Pennsylvania built over a waterfall, exemplifying Wright's philosophy of integrating architecture with nature.

q: Helmut Jahn (1940–2021) was known for combining which two design sensibilities?
n: The German American architect Jahn was known for his high-tech and postmodern designs, such as the James R. Thompson Center (1985) in Chicago.

q: During which years was the Manila Carnival held, for which the Manila Carnival Architects designed pavilions?
ref: Architectural Groups (Local), The Manila Carnival Architects
n: The Manila Carnival Architects designed the elaborate pavilions and structures for the Manila Carnival (1908–1939), testing Neo-Classical and Art Deco styles.

q: Which building is Jørn Utzon (1918–2008) best known for?
n: Utzon is renowned for designing the iconic Sydney Opera House in Australia, celebrated for its innovative use of sculptural forms.

q: Which architect was a key collaborator, not a founding member, of the Memphis Group?
n: Michael Graves, along with Hans Hollein, Shiro Kuramata, Arata Isozaki, and Peter Shire, was a Key Collaborator of the Memphis Group; the Core Members/Founders included Sottsass, Martine Bedin, Aldo Cibic, Michele De Lucchi, Nathalie Du Pasquier, Matteo Thun, and George J. Sowden.

q: Peter Eisenman treats architecture as a form of what, as in his 'deconstructed grid' at the Memorial to the Murdered Jews of Europe?
n: Eisenman, known for his deconstructivism approach, views architecture as a form of linguistics and is famous for deconstructing the grid, creating complex, fragmented spaces.

q: Which Paris cultural center did Renzo Piano (b. 1937) co-design?
n: Piano co-designed the Centre Georges Pompidou in Paris, known for its exposed structural elements.

q: Hector Guimard (1867–1942) is best known for which ironwork designs?
n: Guimard's Paris Métro Entrances (early 1900s), with sinuous cast-iron designs and floral motifs, became synonymous with the Art Nouveau movement.

q: Sir Christopher Wren (1632–1723) helped rebuild London after which event?
n: Wren was instrumental in rebuilding London after the Great Fire of 1666; his works, including St. Paul's Cathedral, are characterized by classical architecture infused with Baroque elements.

q: Which architect is known to have said: "My hand is the extension of the thinking process—the creative process"?
n: "My hand is the extension of the thinking process—the creative process" is a dictum of Tadao Ando (b. 1941).

q: Which London tower, nicknamed 'The Gherkin', did Norman Foster design?
n: Foster's notable works include 30 St Mary Axe (The Gherkin), London—a distinctive, energy-efficient skyscraper.

q: The Metabolist Group was formed for which 1960 event in Tokyo?
n: The Metabolist Group was officially formed for the 1960 World Design Conference in Tokyo, drafting the manifesto 'Metabolism: The Proposals for a New Urbanism.'

q: Which concept did Frank Lloyd Wright develop, rejecting rooms as single-purpose boxes?
n: Wright developed the idea of the Prairie house, rejecting existing views of rooms as single-function boxes and creating overlapping, interpenetrating rooms with shared spaces.

q: Which architect is on record with the statement: "Architecture is about understanding the world and turning it into a more meaningful and humane place"?
n: This dictum belongs to Jørn Utzon (1918–2008).

q: Who was the first pensionado architect, graduating from Drexel Institute in 1908?
n: Carlos Barretto was the first pensionado architect, graduating from Drexel Institute in 1908.

q: What distinction does Inigo Jones's Banqueting House (1619) in Whitehall hold?
o: It's the first Gothic Revival building in England
It's the first building in England designed in a pure classical style
It's the tallest building in England at the time
n: The Banqueting House (1619) is the first building in England designed in a pure classical style.

q: Otto Wagner (1841–1918) was a key figure in which Austrian movement?
n: The Austrian architect and urban planner Wagner was a key figure in the Vienna Secession movement and a pioneer of modern architecture in Austria.

q: Fumihiko Maki's idea of 'Group Form' proposes that buildings should be what?
o: Single megastructures fixed in their final form
Identical boxes repeated along a strict grid
Clusters of parts that can grow and change over time
Towers set apart in open parkland
n: Maki is known for 'Group Form'—the idea that buildings should be designed as a cluster of parts that can grow and change over time, rather than a fixed, singular object.

q: Which architect said: "As an architect, you design for the present, with an awareness of the past, for a future which is essentially unknown"?
n: This dictum belongs to Norman Foster (b. 1935).

q: For which Arts and Crafts figure did Philip Webb (1831–1915) design the Red House in Bexleyheath?
n: Webb, a key figure in the Arts and Crafts movement, designed the Red House in Bexleyheath for William Morris; it's considered a seminal Arts and Crafts residence.

q: Which aphorism did Ludwig Mies van der Rohe (1886–1969) make famous?
ref: Famous Architects, Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
n: The German-American architect Mies is known for his minimalist designs and the aphorism 'less is more.'

q: Pablo S. Antonio (National Artist, 1976), pioneer of modern Philippine architecture, emphasized what?
o: Massive concrete structures with long eaves
Clean lines, plain surfaces, natural light, and ventilation
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Pablo S. Antonio
n: Pablo S. Antonio is considered the pioneer of modern Philippine architecture, with work characterized by clean lines, plain surfaces, and a focus on natural light and ventilation.

q: Which architect made the remark: "If we learn to build with local materials, we have a future"?
n: This dictum belongs to Francis Kéré (b. 1965).

q: Which approach does Aldo Rossi's San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena show?
n: San Cataldo Cemetery in Modena, Italy, showcases Rossi's metaphysical approach to architecture.

q: Which of these is a work of National Artist Juan F. Nakpil?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Juan F. Nakpil
n: Nakpil's notable works include Quiapo Church (reconstruction and expansion), UP Administration and Library buildings (Quezon Hall), Capitol Theater Manila, and the Rizal Shrine, Calamba (reconstruction).

q: Which architect is on record with the statement: "Architects don't invent anything; they transform reality"?
n: "Architects don't invent anything; they transform reality" and "Tradition is a challenge to innovation" are dicta of Alvaro Siza Vieira (b. 1933).

q: Which of these is a work of Eero Saarinen?
n: Eero Saarinen's notable works include the TWA Flight Center at JFK Airport, the Gateway Arch in St. Louis, and Dulles International Airport.

q: Which architect is known to have said: "A Doctor can bury his mistakes, but an architect can only advise his client to plant vines"?
n: This dictum belongs to Frank Lloyd Wright (1867–1959).

q: Which architect made the remark: "Architecture should speak of its time and place but yearn for timelessness"?
n: This dictum belongs to Frank Gehry (b. 1929).

q: Richard Meier (b. 1934), one of 'The New York Five', is known for what signature?
o: Pristine white buildings and geometric designs
n: Meier, associated with 'The New York Five,' is known for his pristine white buildings and geometric designs that emphasize light and space, such as the Getty Center.

q: Which pensionado, the most prolific of the group, designed the Manila Central Post Office and the Metropolitan Theater?
n: Juan Arellano, known as the most prolific among the pensionados, designed the Manila Central Post Office and the Metropolitan Theater.

q: Which design school did Walter Gropius (1883–1969) found?
n: Gropius, a German architect, was the founder of the Bauhaus School, a key figure in modernist architecture promoting functional design and the integration of art, craft, and technology.

q: Which architect is credited with the line: "Less is more"?
ref: Architects' dictums, Ludwig Mies van der Rohe
n: "Less is more" (and "God is in the details") are famous dicta of Ludwig Mies van der Rohe (1886–1969).

q: Philip Johnson (1906–2005) helped bring modernism to the U.S. and later embraced which movement?
n: Johnson was a key figure in the introduction of modernist architecture to the U.S. and later embraced postmodernism, as seen in his AT&T Building (now Sony Tower).

q: During which period were the pensionados sent to the United States as government scholars?
n: The Pensionados were the first Filipino architects sent to the United States as government scholars (pensionados) during the American colonial period, to study Neo-Classical and Beaux-Arts style.

q: Which housing complex best shows Moshe Safdie's humanistic, community-centered approach?
n: Safdie's Habitat '67 in Montreal is a revolutionary housing complex that reimagined urban living, reflecting his humanistic approach.

q: Which practice did Rem Koolhaas (b. 1944) found?
n: Koolhaas founded the Office for Metropolitan Architecture (OMA) and has influenced contemporary architecture through both practice and theory.

q: Which architect is on record with the statement: "Yes is more"?
n: "Yes is more" is the well-known dictum of Bjarke Ingels (b. 1974).

q: Kisho Kurokawa's Nakagin Capsule Tower emphasized what?
o: Flexibility and organic growth in architecture
n: Kurokawa's designs, including the Nakagin Capsule Tower in Tokyo, emphasized flexibility and organic growth in architecture.

q: The Bauhaus, founded by Walter Gropius in 1919, was led by a body known as what?
n: The Bauhaus school, founded by Walter Gropius in 1919, was led by a 'Council of Masters' who integrated craft, art, and technology.

q: Marcel Breuer moved from furniture such as the Wassily Chair to monumental buildings in which material and style?
n: Breuer popularized the use of heavy, textured 'beton brut' (raw concrete) and the cantilever in residential architecture, transitioning from furniture design to monumental Brutalism.

q: Paul Rudolph (1918–1997), former dean of the Yale School of Architecture, is known for contributions to which movement?
n: Rudolph was known for his bold, complex designs and contributions to the Brutalist movement, as seen in the Yale Art and Architecture Building.

q: Which of these is NOT a work of Alvar Aalto?
n: Fallingwater is a Frank Lloyd Wright work, not Aalto's. Aalto's notable works include Säynätsalo Town Hall, Paimio Sanatorium, and Villa Mairea.

q: Leandro V. Locsin, the 'Poet of Space', designed massive concrete structures that seem to do what?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Leandro V. Locsin
n: Locsin, nicknamed the 'Poet of Space,' mastered heavy materials made to look ethereal—massive concrete that appears to 'float.'

q: Eliel Saarinen (1873–1950) is first recognized for contributions to which style?
n: Eliel Saarinen is recognized for his contributions to Art Nouveau architecture and later his influence on modernist design in the United States, with notable works like Helsinki Central Railway Station.

q: Which of these is a landscape work of National Artist Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.
n: Santos's landscape works include the San Miguel Building (Ortigas, Pasig City), Luneta Park (Manila), Tagaytay Highlands (Cavite), and Paco Park (Manila, renovation).

q: 'The New York Five' ('The Whites') shared an obsession with the pure white forms of which early modernist?
ref: Architectural Groups (International), The New York Five
n: The New York Five ('The Whites') shared an obsession with the pure, white, geometric forms of early Le Corbusier, and were featured in the 1972 book 'Five Architects.'

q: Which architect is associated with the words: "The straight line belongs to men, the curved one to God"?
n: "The straight line belongs to men, the curved one to God" is a dictum of Antoni Gaudí (1852–1926).

q: Hexagon Architects, named for its six members, was formed to design which Manila building?
o: The National Library of the Philippines
The Cultural Center of the Philippines
n: Hexagon Architects was formed to handle the design and execution of the National Library of the Philippines in Manila, named 'Hexagon' for its six prominent architects.

q: Which pensionado was the first registered architect in the Philippines and founded the Mapua Institute of Technology?
n: Tomas Mapua was the first registered architect in the Philippines and founder of Mapua Institute of Technology.

q: Which member of The New York Five later turned to Postmodernism?
ref: Architectural Groups (International), The New York Five
n: Michael Graves was a member of The New York Five who later pivoted to Postmodernism; the group also included Peter Eisenman, Charles Gwathmey, John Hejduk, and Richard Meier.

q: What is Gaudí's mosaic technique of broken tile pieces called?
n: Trencadís is Gaudí's decorative technique using broken mosaic pieces.

q: Oscar Niemeyer's curving modernist buildings define the identity of which city?
n: Niemeyer's curvaceous modernist buildings, including the Cathedral of Brasília and the National Congress of Brazil, are integral to the identity of Brasília, Brazil's capital.

q: Which building with its services exposed outside did Richard Rogers (1933–2021) co-design?
n: Rogers co-designed the Centre Pompidou and is also known for the Lloyd's Building, London, which features services exposed on the exterior.

q: Ildefonso P. Santos Jr. (National Artist, 2006), 'IP Santos', is regarded as what?
ref: National Artist for Architecture, Ildefonso P. Santos Jr.
n: Ildefonso P. Santos Jr. is regarded as the 'Father of Philippine Landscape Architecture,' pioneering the practice of landscape architecture in the Philippines.

q: Which concept of designing in harmony with people and nature did Frank Lloyd Wright champion?
n: The iconic American architect Wright championed the concept of 'organic architecture,' designing more than 1,000 structures over his 70-year career.

q: What is the urban revival credited to Gehry's Guggenheim Museum Bilbao called?
n: The Guggenheim Museum Bilbao (1997), a titanium-clad museum credited with revitalizing the city, gave rise to the phenomenon termed the 'Bilbao Effect.'

q: Which architect is known to have said: "We are called the architects of the future, not its victims"?
n: "We are called the architects of the future, not its victims" and "Doing more with less" are dicta of Buckminster Fuller (1895–1983).

q: Frei Otto (1925–2015) was a pioneer of which type of structure?
n: The German architect and structural engineer Otto was a pioneer in lightweight and tensile structures, and developed a convertible roof with variable geometry, as seen at the Munich Olympic Stadium (1972).

q: Erich Mendelsohn (1887–1953), who designed without historical precedent, pioneered which movement?
n: The German architect Mendelsohn was a pioneer of Expressionist architecture and later contributed to the International Style, using no historical precedents in his designs. His Einstein Tower in Potsdam is a notable example.

q: In which country is Geoffrey Bawa's Heritance Kandalama Hotel?
n: The Heritance Kandalama Hotel in Dambulla, Sri Lanka, built into a rocky cliff overlooking the Kandalama Tank and Sigiriya Rock, is considered one of Bawa's greatest masterpieces.

q: The Memphis Group, founded by Ettore Sottsass in Milan in 1980, reacted against what?
n: The Memphis Group, founded by Ettore Sottsass in 1980, reacted against the 'good taste' of Modernism.

q: Louis Sullivan (1856–1924), key figure of the Chicago School, is often called what?
n: Sullivan is often referred to as the 'Father of skyscrapers,' was a key figure in the Chicago School, and was also considered the 'Dean of American Architects.'

q: Benjamin Henry Latrobe (1764–1820) is often called what?
n: The English-born American architect Latrobe is often referred to as the 'father of American architecture' and introduced Greek Revival architecture to the United States.

q: In which year was the Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) founded?
ref: Architectural Groups (Local), The Philippine Institute of Architects (PIA) Founders
n: The PIA was founded in 1933 as the first professional organization for architects in the Philippines, with founding members including Juan Nakpil, Tomas Mapua, Tomas Arguelles, Andres Luna de San Pedro, and Carlos Barretto.

q: Minoru Yamasaki (1912–1986) is best known for designing which structure?
o: The original World Trade Center towers
The Empire State Building in New York
The Chrysler Building in New York
n: Yamasaki designed the World Trade Center Twin Towers in New York City, once the tallest buildings in the world and iconic symbols of the city.

q: Which Austrian firm, led by Wolf Prix and Helmut Swiczinsky, was in the 1988 MoMA Deconstructivist exhibition?
n: Coop Himmelb(l)au, the Austrian firm led by Wolf Prix and Helmut Swiczinsky, was among the Deconstructivists.

q: Louis Sullivan was mentor to which other great American architect?
n: Sullivan was a mentor to Frank Lloyd Wright.
